title: The poet who reshaped a lake
summary: Su Causeway is more than a scenic walk. In the late eleventh century, Su Shi, also known as Su Dongpo, served as Hangzhou’s governor and directed work to dredge West Lake. Silt removed from the water became a causeway across it. The poet’s name now belongs to a piece of public engineering: a path that connects the lake’s beauty with the practical work of caring for a city.

sections.heading: A landscape made by people
sections.text: The ICOMOS evaluation of West Lake dates this dredging to 1090 and describes six bridges along the causeway. Hangzhou’s city guide connects the project with Su’s work as a poet and administrator. The path is a reminder that a celebrated landscape can also be shaped by water management. It is not simply untouched nature.
